title: Glute bridge progression: five rungs from the floor to one leg
caption: Glute bridge progression from two legs to one: five rungs, each with its reps and the test that says you are ready for the next. Nothing but the floor and a kitchen chair, and quiet enough for a sleeping kid next door. Save the ladder.

overlays.text: A glute bridge looks like nothing. Five rungs later it is on one leg.
Glute Bridge. 10 reps. Feet flat on the floor, lift your hips, lower slow.

scenes.footer: Ready when your hips stay level in the pause.

overlays.text: Paused Glute Bridge. 8 reps. Lift your hips, hold two seconds, lower slow.

scenes.footer: Ready when all 10 reach the same height.

overlays.text: Feet-Elevated Glute Bridge. 10 reps. Heels on a chair, lift your hips, lower.

scenes.footer: Ready when both sides feel the same.

overlays.text: Single-Leg Glute Bridge. 8 reps each side. One foot down, other knee up, lift.

scenes.footer: Ready when you can hold the top for two seconds.

overlays.text: Single-Leg Elevated Bridge. 6 reps each side. One heel on the chair, lift.
The top rung takes months, not a week.
